subject: Next steps: dedicated pool qualification & isolation matrix
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mike Ramirez <mike.ramirez@deepsearobotics.com>, Chris Monroe <chris.monroe@deepsearobotics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call notes + ask: dedicated pool qualification & isolation matrix

Hi Mike / Chris —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Short recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so we have a clear handoff:

High-level goals you shared:
- Stable inference for customer-facing features (low tail latency during peak video-annotation bursts)
- Data isolation for customer models and PII/PHI (compliance with internal policy for robotic telemetry)
- Predictable unit economics for scale (we need to understand cost per 100k tokens at target throughput)

Primary pain observed today:
- P95 latency spikes when batch jobs overlap with real-time requests (multi-tenant contention)
- Occasional model warmup storms that push memory/kv-cache eviction
- Need for private networking (VPN or VPC peering) and customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest

What we propose based on the call:
1) Qualification matrix: provision a dedicated pool (initially 4xA100 equivalent slots) with strict tenant isolation (segregated pools + prefix KV caching) and a burst lane for sudden traffic surges.
2) SLA targets: target 99.95% availability for the pool and p95 gen latency <200ms at 512 tokens for single-request workloads; fallbacks to smaller, cheaper quantized variants on overload.
3) Security: support for customer-managed KMS, VPC peering or private link, and audit logs exported to your SIEM.
4) Timeline & decision path: pilot (3 weeks smoke + 4 weeks load validation) → procurement sign-off → reserved commit (quarterly billing or annual commit).

Next actions (owner / due):
- DeepSea: share a week of anonymized production tail traces (aggregate token counts + p95/p99 samples) — Chris (due: Tue 30 Jun)
- Redwood: produce a sizing matrix and cost estimate for 3 pool shapes (4xA100, 8xA100, 4xH100) + draft SLA — Priyom (due: Wed 1 Jul) [attached: sizing matrix]
- Security / legal: we will circulate the SOC2/pen test artifacts and a network sketch — Ben to own delivery (due: Thu 2 Jul)
- Schedule: technical deep-dive (infrastructure + ops) with your infra team — proposed windows Wed 7 Jul or Thu 8 Jul — Laura to coordinate

I attached the initial sizing workbook and a quick network isolation sketch. If anything above is incorrect or missing, flag it and I’ll update.

Thanks,
Priyom

Priyom —

Appreciate the clear recap. Confirming a few things from our side:

- We can share aggregated traces (no customer-identifiable payloads) but it will take security a day to scrub. Chris will send by EOD Tue 30 Jun.
- Our procurement cadence is relatively fast this quarter; if the pilot looks good we can sign a 12-month reserve in July.
- A couple of security asks up-front: do you support HSM-backed KMS (Y/N)? Do you have a recommended VPC peering pattern for our multi-region clusters?
- On sizing: the burst lane is important. During demos we see 3x normal traffic for 5–10 minute windows; that’s what caused the p95 spikes.

Can you also provide a rough top-line cost band for the three shapes you mentioned (ballpark monthly committed cost)? We need something for our headcount planning.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Mike

Mike / team — quick answers and plan: 

- HSM-backed KMS: yes — we support customer-provided keys via AWS CloudHSM / external HSM integration; I'll attach the KMS integration checklist to the HubSpot record.
- Peering pattern: for multi-region we recommend VPC peering into a dedicated VPC per region with a transit gateway for cross-region routing; will bring diagram to the deep-dive.
- Cost band (ballpark monthly committed):
  - 4xA100 shape: ~$45k–55k / month committed
  - 8xA100 shape: ~$85k–100k / month committed
  - 4xH100 shape: ~$120k–150k / month committed
  (we'll refine once we see traces and token mix)
